main_text.head: APODICTICA CAUSSÆ DEMONSTRATIO Per collocationem IMPLEMENTI Cum re SPERATA.
main_text.p: §. 1.IN sermone hoc prophetico vates ad Deum defert spem Patrum de salute per Christum adducenda, atque eleganter depingit, quanto cum desiderii fervore eam rem petierint, ad hanc gratiam anhelantes, atque in eâ re spera a unicum fidei fundamentum collocantes. In hoc tempus proin inquisiverunt serio, & non sine gemitibus illud novisse à Deo petierunt: quod non solum Petrus testatur, (1 Petr. 1: 10.) verum etiam praesens querelæ[?] delineatio comprobat. Neque id frustra sperasse evicit rei eventus: venit enim in plenitudine temporis ille, cui ab ista salute nomen impositum est; quod non humano factum fuisse arbitrio, sed mandato divino, mediante angelica legatione, id nomen praescribente & simul ex causa ἱστορίας[?] exponente: sic enim e-

page.notes: The printed running head reads "HABAKUK" with "CAP. I. 14." beside it at top right; only the title is given as running head, the chapter and verse reference is omitted. Doubtful: "spera a unicum" (perhaps a misprint for "spem"); "tempus proin" as printed; "querelæ" is hard to read; the Greek word after "causa" is partly obscured and is marked [?]. Hyphenated "e-" at the line end continues as the catchword "nim" (the line-end word "enim"). The paragraph is set in the 1st-person margin mark "§. 1." which stands outside the text block.
